QUESTION:
Which setting determines how much memory the part that holds back messages until a later point in time reserves for buffering?

DOCUMENTATION EXCERPTS:
[d0826] config | partitioner.buffer_bytes | version 4.x
# `partitioner.buffer_bytes`

> Configuration reference for PaderQueue 4.x (current).

Size of the in-memory buffer used by the partitioner that decides into which partition a message is written, in bytes.

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Type | integer (bytes) |
| Default | `16777216` |
| Available since | 2.0 |
| Component | partitioner |
| Unit | bytes |
| Default changed | in 3.0 (see release notes) |

## When to change it

The default works for most deployments. Change `partitioner.buffer_bytes` only if you observe problems with the partitioner that decides into which partition a message is written, for example in the metrics dashboard.

Set it in `paderqueue.toml`:

```toml
[partitioner]
buffer_bytes = 16777216
```

[d0899] config | partitioner.buffer_bytes (PaderQueue 2.x) | version 2.x
# `partitioner.buffer_bytes` (PaderQueue 2.x)

> Configuration reference for PaderQueue 2.x.

Size of the in-memory buffer used by the partitioner that decides into which partition a message is written, in bytes.

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Type | integer (bytes) |
| Default | `1048576` |
| Available since | 2.0 |
| Component | partitioner |
| Unit | bytes |

## Notes

Changes to `partitioner.buffer_bytes` take effect after restarting the node. In clusters, use the same value on all nodes.

Set it in `paderqueue.toml`:

```toml
[partitioner]
buffer_bytes = 1048576
```

# PaderQueue 2.3 release notes

Released on 2023-03-27.

## New features

- New option `scheduler.buffer_bytes`: size of the in-memory buffer used by the scheduler that releases delayed messages at their due time, in bytes.

- New error code PQ-E4540 (METRICS_CONNECTION_LIMIT_REACHED) with a clearer log message.

- New error code PQ-E1163 (SNAPSHOTTER_CONNECTION_LIMIT_REACHED) with a clearer log message.

- New option `auth.threshold_percent`: usage level in percent at which the authentication module that validates client tokens starts throttling.

- New option `partitioner.log_level`: log verbosity of the partitioner that decides into which partition a message is written.

- New option `quota.timeout_ms`: time in milliseconds that the quota manager that limits the throughput per tenant waits for a response before the operation fails.

response.content: The setting is `scheduler.buffer_bytes`. It controls the scheduler’s in-memory buffer for delayed messages, in bytes.
